# Activation baseline-concern checklist (generated)

When a project is activated onto the kernel it is walked through the baseline concerns below —
one row per concern whose spec DECLARED an `init_question` — forcing declare-or-waive on each
(opt-out always available). Both views derive from the SAME declarations, so a new concern spec
that declares its `init_question` AUTO-APPEARS here with no hand edit (SPEC-0096).

## Init-walk SET

The machine set the interactive `init` walk presents — one concern row per declared
concern, keyed by spec id so the walk can resolve each. owns the walk; this is only the SET.

- **SPEC-0094** (`universal`) → Does this project deploy a change to a live serving surface — and if so, what is its governed `deploy:` command, and how is each user-facing change probed live before close (the per-change live_probe)? Declare the deploy seam + live-probe, or waive.
- **SPEC-0097** (`universal`) → Does this project deploy AUTONOMOUSLY — the AI runs the governed `deploy` verb without an extra per-deploy owner approval, gated only when a change's worst case is not acceptably reversible within the project's RTO/RPO (the A/S/C1/C2 classification)? Declare the `deploy.policy` block (its per-class evidence + any per-class waivers), or waive to stay owner-gated on every deploy.
- **SPEC-0099** (`universal`) → Does this project keep secrets / credential-bearing material OUT of every durable artifact (the append-only `events.jsonl` journal, committed docs, diffs, probe output / acceptance evidence) AND out of external-auditor payloads? Acknowledge the no-secrets-in-durable-artifacts NOW-rule (input-side discipline — the irreversible channel stays clean), or waive.
- **SPEC-0100** (`universal`) → When authoring a user-facing interaction (a delete button, a form submit, a money action), does this project FILL the relevant cross-project behavioral/UX-safety DEFAULT (e.g. confirm-before-irreversible) from the catalog `patterns/behavioral-baseline-defaults.md` into its own spec — instead of re-deriving the rule from an incident? Adopt the behavioral-baseline defaults, or waive.
- **SPEC-0125** (`universal`) → Is this project's substantive operating-context (product profile, module map, integration constraints, safety bans, PII policy) FILLED into the ONE declared provider-neutral home the thin vendor adapter points at — product `CHARTER.md` if present, else the born project `AGENTS.md` (Rule 1) — rather than left as the born `<fill in …>` stub or accreted into the vendor `<vendor-adapter>.md`? Fill the neutral home, or waive with a named explicit waiver (never a silent empty stub).
- **SPEC-0135** (`universal`) → Does this project POPULATE its.yitc/transcript-archive (the kernel Duty-1 recipe: rsync -a ~/<provider-config>/projects/ <repo>/.yitc/transcript-archive) so the read-time token-rollup COST dimension (baseline $/task) is measurable? Declare the population duty, or waive the cost dimension.
- **SPEC-0145** (`universal`) → Does this project have a security surface that must be audited on a cadence — and if so, what is its provider-independent system trigger (`cadence:`), its gate freshness window (`freshness_sla:`), and the deterministic `runner:` that produces the evidence report? Declare `security.audit`, or waive (STRICT).
- **SPEC-0163** (`universal`) → Does this project SYNC to a git remote — and if so, WHICH remote (`remote:`), WHO pushes to it (`pusher:` — a real named identity, not a retired system's auto-pusher), and is CI LIVE on the far side and in what ROLE (`ci:` — a blocking GATE, or an extra check beside `verify.layers`)? Declare `remote_sync` (all three — they are one stance), or waive.

The human-readable companion — each concern's prompt, what a bare waiver may omit, the governed
adoption-evidence pointer that proves it handled, and its tier.
